proposals.statement:
theorem periodicFrom_trans_period (f : ℕ → Bool) (p q N M : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p)
    (hN : PeriodicFrom f p N) (hM : PeriodicFrom f q M) : PeriodicFrom f q N := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: Every onset argument converts 'some period from an early onset' into 'the specific period 2^k from that early onset', and this is that conversion; it is private in LeftDiagonalOnsetLeIffRowNatReturn.lean and in two parked wall attempts, and a proof of the wall via any of the reductions cites it to read the wall's conclusion off a return with a different period.
proposals.disclaims: A statement about Bool sequences, not about rule 30; it bears on no wall by itself.

route.tactics:
intro n hn
  have hMp : M ≤ M * p := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right M hp
  have h1 := periodicFrom_mul f p N hN M (n + q) (by omega)
  have h2 := periodicFrom_mul f p N hN M n hn
  have h3 := hM (n + M * p) (by omega)
  rw [← h1, ← h2, ← h3]
  congr 1
  omega

proposals.statement:
theorem leftDiagonal_white_succ_iff (m i : ℕ) (hw : leftDiagonal (m + 2) i = false) :
    leftDiagonal (m + 2) (i + 1) = false ↔
      leftDiagonal m (i + 2) = leftDiagonal (m + 1) (i + 1) := by
  sorry
proposals.reason: A frozen step of the settled boundary is a white cell on the diagonal just inside it, and this is the exact law of when the next step is frozen too: the white run continues iff the two diagonals beneath agree, which is the hypothesis leftDiagonal_agree_succ_iff cascades from; a proof of the wall bounding frozen runs cites it at every run.
proposals.disclaims: Local mechanism only; it bounds no run length and proves nothing about any onset.

route.tactics:
rw [leftDiagonal_recurrence, hw]
  cases leftDiagonal m (i + 2) <;> cases leftDiagonal (m + 1) (i + 1) <;> decide
